statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register and separate International Companies register (online portal: Connect Online via https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be in Roman/Latin alphabet characters; the Registrar accepts Māori macron diacritics and phonetically transliterates these to ASCII index equivalents for search functionality; names must be distinguishable from all existing registered names, must not suggest a misleading legal entity status, and must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd.', or 'Tapui' (Māori) where liability is limited; a virtual brand trade name in a non-Latin script may be displayed commercially, but the statutory registered name must have a mechanically transliterated English/Roman equivalent entered on the public register at all times.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal refusal of a proposed name, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Companies Office Settlements Team within 15 working days, identifying why the name is not confusingly similar or misleading under the Companies Act 1993; reconsideration decisions are rendered ex parte; if reconsideration remains adverse, the applicant may invoke the administrative review power of the Registrar of Companies and, alternatively or subsequently, may issue proceedings for judicial review before the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016, naming the Registrar as respondent and seeking an order for statutory reconsideration; no filing fee attaches to the first reconsideration request, and the full judicial review route is subject to strict 28-day filing timelines once the final administrative decision is issued.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A grandfathered New Zealand International Company must maintain a physical registered office address in New Zealand at which legal process may be served during ordinary business hours; a virtual office or mail-forwarding box is not acceptable as the sole registered office where the entity carries on regulated food-trading activities; however, a virtual administrative address is permissible for commercial correspondence and delivery-platform notices provided that the operational ghost kitchen maintains a separately registered physical food premises under the Food Act 2014.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 42% (estimated aggregate probability of at least one unannounced physical on-site inspection during the first two years of operation by the Ministry for Primary Industries or the territorial authority under the Food Act 2014 risk-based verification framework; the probability escalates above 50% where consumer complaint volume is elevated or the online food-safety rating deteriorates across the virtual brands).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), specifically sections 12 (incorporation by registration), 15 (constitution), 16 (manner of incorporation), 23 (share capital and classes of shares), 37 (financial assistance for acquisition of shares, where applicable), and 122 (appointment of directors). For overseas-owned entities, the Overseas Investment Act 2005 may apply if significant business assets are acquired, but is not triggered by mere incorporation of a shelf international company used for delivery-only operations; the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 does not apply to a private company with no public offer of securities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); online portal at companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCO-1: Application for Incorporation / Registration of a Company (electronic filing via the Companies Office online register).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a New Zealand company under the Companies Act 1993. The company may issue shares with a par value of nil or nominal value (NZD 0.01 per share) without an escrow account requirement. If a constitution restricts share transfers for the ghost kitchen holding vehicle, a shareholder resolution adopting the constitution is required. For the Tax Exempt Zone classification referenced in the internal metadata, a pure non-resident-owned international company that elects to be a 'company deriving exempt income' under section CW 9 or an 'overseas company' branch may qualify for tax exemption only if it conducts business outside New Zealand and satisfies the Offshore Company rules; no capital escrow is required by the Companies Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company'), adopted in writing by unanimous resolution of the Board of Directors on [DATE] pursuant to section 91 of the Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand) and clause [X] of the Company's Constitution. RESOLVED: (1) SHARE CAPITAL: That the issue and allotment of [NUMBER] fully paid ordinary shares and [NUMBER] [Class B management/administration] shares, as set out in the share application schedule attached hereto, be and is hereby approved, and that the registered holders thereof be recorded in the Company's Register of Members at a consideration of NZD [0.01] per share, and that such consideration be satisfied by payment in full, with no calls or instalments outstanding. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE: That the registered office of the Company be established at [Address], Auckland / Wellington / Christchurch, New Zealand, that such address be filed with the Registrar of Companies as the Company's registered office, and that [Name] be appointed as the person authorised to accept service of legal process on behalf of the Company within New Zealand. (3) OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: That the following persons be and are hereby appointed as directors and officers of the Company for the ensuing year: [Name], Director; [Name], Chief Executive Officer; [Name], Chief Financial Officer; and [Name], Company Secretary (if any), each to serve until annual reappointment or earlier removal in accordance with the Company's Constitution and the Companies Act 1993. (4) BANK ACCOUNT AUTHORITY: That the Company Secretary be and is hereby directed to open a bank account in the Company's name and that any two of the Directors shall jointly sign as authorised signatories, with online banking mandates limited to pre-approved payout providers (UberEats and DoorDash). (5) FILING OF INCORPORATION: That the Company Secretary be directed to complete and submit Form NZCO-1 to the New Zealand Companies Office, to pay the registration fee, and to receive the Certificate of Incorporation and the Company's New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). RESOLVED FURTHER that the above resolutions take effect immediately and that a copy of this resolution be placed in the Company's minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO) online name availability search, accessed via the New Zealand Business Number Register and Companies Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name search using the NZCO 'Name Availability' tool. Ensure that the proposed company name (e.g., '[Brand] Virtual Kitchen Operations NZ Limited') is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, reserved name, or trade mark on the New Zealand Trade Marks Register (IPONZ). If the desired name is available, reserve it electronically for up to 20 business days (where user-customer support is available) or proceed immediately to incorporation. For a company intended to operate only as a tax-exempt international company, the name may not contain words implying affiliation with the Crown, a government body, or a regulated profession unless prior consent is obtained. If the name is refused, submit a written request to NZCO for a reconsideration, or adopt a variant with a distinctive prefix or geographic qualifier.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and list of three alternative names
Proof of identity details of proposed directors and shareholders (passport copies not required at reservation stage)
IPONZ trade mark search report (internal due diligence, not filed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusing similarity, file a new online name search with a materially distinct name or file a formal objection/submission under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993 if the name is already in use and the applicant claims a superior right; alternatively, obtain written consent from the existing name holder and attach it to Form NZCO-1.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and adoption of constitution, shareholder and director consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators/authorised agents; no filing with NZCO is made at this stage unless adopting one of the statutory default constitution provisions (in which case the Companies Act 1993 applies by default).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a bespoke constitution for the company in accordance with section 15-16 of the Companies Act 1993, tailoring it to the ghost kitchen international company structure: use a foreign currency currency model if desired, allow director's indemnity, permit remote director meetings by videoconference, restrict share transfers to maintain eligibility for tax-exempt zone treatment if intended, and set an unlimited share capital. The constitution must be signed by each person who is to be a shareholder, or by the sole incorporator. Alternatively, the Companies Act 1993 'Table of Default Provisions' applies automatically to the extent the constitution does not exclude them. Obtain signed consents to act as directors from each proposed appointee (Form NZCO-? 'Consent to Act as Director'), and signed declarations of eligibility (not disqualified under sections 151-153 of the Companies Act 1993). If any director is not in New Zealand, an agent for service on behalf of the director may be required for the purposes of the Companies Act; the company may appoint a local agent for service. Ensure that the first shareholder resolution (or unanimous written shareholder resolution) authorising the board to allot shares and adopt the constitution is executed before filing if constitution matters are not covered by the default rules.
required_dossiers: Constitution of the company (original signed copy)
Consents to act as director (signed by each director)
Shareholder resolution adopting constitution and authorising allotment of shares
Shareholder register initial entries (draft)
Proof of identity (passport) for each director and shareholder; utility bill or bank statement for address verification
For non-resident directors: certified confirmation of no disqualification in their home jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any consent is defective, the director must file a corrected consent with NZCO as soon as discovered; a failure to obtain proper consent does not invalidate the incorporation but may expose the company to a late filing penalty of NZD 10 per day under the Companies Act, and the director may be deemed not properly appointed unless a retroactive ratification is filed with the Registrar and the Companies Office administrative rectification process under section 156G is used.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of incorporation application Form NZCO-1
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online registration system (NZCO 'Register a Company' portal); payment via NZCO accepted credit/debit cards or client funding account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the Companies Office portal and select 'Register a Company'. Input all required particulars: proposed company name, registered office address (must be a physical address in New Zealand, not a P.O. Box; a director's or agent's address may be used with permission), postal address, address for service of documents, company purpose (must include 'operation of delivery-only cloud kitchen and virtual restaurant brands' and 'provision of food and beverage preparation for third-party delivery platforms' to align with ISIC 5610), share structure (authorised and issued shares, rights attached), director(s) and shareholder(s) details, and the number of shares each subscriber takes. Attach the electronic versions of the constitution and consents to act if not previously uploaded. Complete the applicant declaration, confirming compliance with the Companies Act 1993 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AMLCFT) obligations on the reporting entity (the incorporating agent, if using a licensed agent, must verify identities). Pay the NZD 105.00 fee (currently approx. USD 65.00). Upon successful filing, the Registrar will issue an electronic Certificate of Incorporation and automatically register the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
required_dossiers: Form NZCO-1 (online fields; no scan required) with lodgement declarations
Constitution (electronic copy uploaded, if not previously filed)
Consent to act as director (electronic signatures or hardcopy scanned)
Proof of identification of all directors and shareholders (retained by the filing agent; files may be requested by NZCO in a post-registration monitoring audit)
Residential address details of directors and shareholders (for the Companies Register, but will not be publicly disclosed unless filed under the specific options)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried by the Registrar (e.g., missing statutory declaration, unverifiable director identity, unlawful name, or incomplete constitution), the applicant has 15 business days to cure the defect by filing a further electronic response with corrected particulars. If the Registrar issues a 'Notice of Intention to Refuse', the applicant may request an oral hearing by the Registrar under the Companies Act 1993, section 21(2); the applicant must provide written submissions within 10 working days. If the application is void ab initio due to a fundamental error, a fresh application must be submitted and a refund or credit of the incorporation fee requested; an administrative correction under section 156G may instead be used for minor errors in the company's registered particulars.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation registration of constituent documents and NZBN activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; internal registration by the company's board.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, the board shall within 5 working days prepare and retain the company's statutory registers: (a) register of shares, (b) register of directors, (c) register of ultimate holding company (if any), (d) register of charges (if any), and (e) register of individuals with significant control? (not applicable in NZ; instead, an annual return under section 210 must be filed). The NZBN is automatically created by the Companies Office upon incorporation; activate and validate the NZBN details through the New Zealand Business Number Register. If the company will apply for an IRD number for New Zealand GST and income tax, submit the IRD application to Inland Revenue using the online 'IRD registration for companies' process. Since the target company intends to use UberEats and DoorDash payout rails, register the NZBN and the legal entity details with the Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) Food Safety verification scheme if the company will hold a NZ Food Safety registration or Food Control Plan waiver? (For a ghost kitchen, the operating entity, not merely the holding international company, will need a food business registration under the Food Act 2014; but if the CK_IC is the operating entity, this step mandates registration with MPI/local council).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued by NZCO)
Company's constitution (filed copy from NZCO)
Statutory registers (shareholders, directors, charges)
NZBN notification certificate
IRD number application (Form IRD 596 or online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NZBN or IRD number is delayed, contact the NZ Business Number Register contact centre and Inland Revenue, respectively; if the corporate registers contain errors, file a rectification form with NZCO under section 156G. If the Registrar discovers that the registered office is not a physical address, it will issue a direction to correct; the company should promptly file a change of address and file Form NZCO-2 (Address for Service / Registered Office Change).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting and adoption of corporate governance framework
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board (no government filing required other than updating NZCO with officer changes if any).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, either physically or by video conference, within 10 business days of incorporation. Adopt the pro forma First Board Resolution set out above. Approve the company seal (if any), bank account opening, choice of accounting reference date, adoption of financial control manual, anti-money-laundering compliance programme if the company is a 'reporting entity' under the AMLCFT Act (which is not usually the case for a passive holding company unless it provides trust and company services), and appoint a food safety supervisor (if operating) or designate a third-party facility manager. For a 'ghost kitchen virtual brands' operation, the board should also approve the master licensing agreement with the food delivery platforms (UberEats, DoorDash), and a food safety and quality assurance manual aligned with the Food Act 2014 (Food Control Plan or National Programme). Record the minutes in the company's minute book. Update the Companies Register within 20 working days if a director is replaced or their details change.
required_dossiers: First board resolution (minutes)
Executive officer appointment letters
Bank account application package (Compliance declaration, proof of incorporation, director IDs)
Food safety and quality policy (draft, if operating entity)
Commercial payout provider agreements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If no quorum can be reached due to a director conflict, the board may appoint an additional independent director to achieve a quorum; if a resolution is invalid due to procedural irregularity, the board may pass a subsequent ratification resolution. Any late filing of director changes to NZCO attracts a late filing penalty up to NZD 10.00 per day, so the company should immediately e-file a 'Director Change' form.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: New Zealand hospitality and food safety regulators: (a) local Territorial Authority (city/district council) environmental health and licensing department for food business registration; (b) Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) for national food safety standards and verification; (c) relevant council planning/building departments for resource consent and building code compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operation Licence / Registration under the Food Act 2014, specifically a 'Food Control Plan' registration (or 'National Programme' registration) issued by the applicable Territorial Authority or MPI; plus any required Eating House / Food Premises Permit under local bylaws and, if applicable, a 'Residential/Commercial Food Premises Licence' for a commercial kitchen facility. In Auckland, the licence is issued by Auckland Council under the Food Act 2014 as 'Food Business Registration – Food Control Plan'.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Environment (MFE) and the local Regional Council (e.g., Auckland Council for Auckland region), with the formal environmental assessment process led by the Territorial Authority under the Resource Management Act 1991; for small food premises, no standalone EIA is required unless the kitchen generates significant odour, noise, or discharge, in which case a resource consent and a discharge permit may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 – Registration with a Food Control Plan (no full EIA report required for a standard commercial kitchen operating under a Food Safety Program; however, if the ghost kitchen uses a converted low-density or residential-zoned premise, a resource consent and a full assessment of environmental effects may be required under the local District Plan). [Note: The internal target metadata references ISIC 5610 – food service activities; the operation is not a large industrial process, and therefore no 'Full EIA Report' is mandated.]
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: all kitchen trade wastewater must comply with the regional council 'Trade Waste Bylaw' (e.g., Auckland Council Trade Waste Bylaw 2019), with food grease interceptor (grease trap) installed and maintained; effluent BOD, pH (6.0-8.5), suspended solids, fat/oil/grease concentrations discharging to sewer must not exceed the council's trade waste acceptance thresholds (typically fat/oil/grease ≤ 30 mg/L, BOD ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 400 mg/L, pH 6-10, temperature ≤ 37°C, with prior written approval for any discharge above these). Ventilation/emissions: commercial kitchen ventilation must meet the New Zealand Building Code Clause G4 (Ventilation) and AS/NZS 1668.2 (Mechanical ventilation for food premises); airborne grease emissions to extractor ducting and outdoor air must be filtered with grease filters of not less than 99% efficiency, and odour emitted at the property boundary must not exceed 'no objectionable odour' limits under the Resource Management Act. Waste handling: solid food waste must be stored in vermin-proof, lidded containers and collected by a licensed waste carrier; no food waste may be discharged to stormwater drains; hazardous chemical must be stored in a compliant dangerous goods cabinet with a spill containment bund. Noise: plant and equipment must not exceed the local district plan noise limits (e.g., 50 dBA L10 at night in residential zones) to meet 'reasonable grounds' standards.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety: the operator must obtain a New Zealand Fire Safety Certificate / Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) under the Building Act 2004 and the Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) regulations, including a fire evacuation scheme approved by FENZ (Form: 'Fire Evacuation Scheme' application to FENZ), automatic fire suppression system (cooking range hood suppression system) with a current annual inspection certificate, and fire extinguishers serviced within the last 6 months. Occupational: the premises must obtain a Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) issued by the Territorial Authority through the building owner's Independent Qualified Person (IQP) for all building systems, confirming structural load capacity for commercial kitchen equipment; the operating company must complete an Asbestos Management Plan survey and, if existing, a 'Person Conducting a Business or Undertaking (PCBU)' health and safety register under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. Food safety clearance: all food handlers must hold a Food Safety Training certificate at Level 2 or above (e.g., City & Guilds / NZQA unit standards 167; 'Food Handling' instruction), and the business must have a HACCP-based Food Control Plan template approved by MPI, with a nominated 'Food Safety Supervisor' who is a New Zealand resident. Additionally, if the premises are in a designated high-density building, a structural load evaluation (specific to wall-mounted extraction systems and refrigerator racks) and electrical certificate of compliance for all cooking appliances must be issued by a licensed electrician prior to commencement of operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake), Government of New Zealand; principal statutes: Income Tax Act 2007, Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, Tax Administration Act 1994; primary digital portal: myIR (www.ird.govt.nz); export customs formalities are separately administered by the New Zealand Customs Service through the Trade Single Window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated International Company (CK_IC) that has no fixed establishment in New Zealand must apply to the IRD for a non-resident IRD number (the statutory 8- or 9-digit tax file number) using Form IR742, accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, full board and ownership particulars, AML/CFT beneficial-ownership information, and evidence of tax residence in the jurisdiction of incorporation; the IRD number is the single taxpayer identifier for income tax, GST and PAYE; GST registration is made on Form IR356 and is mandatory once taxable supplies made in or from New Zealand exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period; a non-resident may also be obliged to register for offshore remote-services GST from the first dollar where supplying remote services to New Zealand consumers; registration must be completed before the first taxable period return falls due; engagement of a NZ-resident agent for service of process and the use of licensed tax agents for myIR filing are strongly recommended.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — the CK_IC International Company is classified as a non-resident, non-dual-resident corporate vehicle with no New Zealand fixed establishment or permanent establishment; it is accordingly outside the New Zealand income-tax base for all foreign-sourced income and is taxable only on income having a New Zealand source (standard corporate rate 28% under the Income Tax Act 2007); the label denotes the model classification for this non-residence-driven exemption and does not imply any statutory freeport or territorial tax-incentive zone within New Zealand.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; available statutory elections include: (1) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under Subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007 for closely held NZ-resident companies electing full pass-through tax treatment; (2) the irrevocable non-residence election inherent in the IC template where central management and control remain offshore; (3) New Zealand Foreign Trust (NZFT) election under the Tax Administration Act 1994, exempting the trustee from NZ income tax on foreign-sourced income of a non-resident settlor; (4) Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) election to reduce non-resident withholding tax on interest paid to offshore lenders; (5) hybrid-mismatch countermeasures imposed by Subpart FM of the Income Tax Act 2007 (deduction/no-inclusion, double-deduction and imported-mismatch rules), which eliminate any elective benefit from hybrid instruments or hybrid entities; no dual-consolidation or optional transparency other than LTC is available to the CK_IC structure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a broad-based value added tax levied under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, incorporating registration, input-credit and zero-rating provisions
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 per rolling 12-month period for persons carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand (section 51, GST Act 1985); voluntary registration is permitted below this threshold; non-resident suppliers of remote services (electronically supplied services) to NZ consumers must register from the first dollar; non-resident suppliers of low-value goods (goods valued NZD 1,000 and below) must register only where supplies to NZ consumers exceed NZD 60,000 per annum; for the ghost-kitchen model, domestic NZ food and beverage sales through UberEats and DoorDash payouts are taxable supplies subject to the standard NZD 60,000 threshold unless the sales are exported.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, pre-clearance API, digital stamping, or tax-authority invoice authorisation mandate exists in New Zealand; e-invoicing is voluntary through the IRD's PEPPOL-based e-Invoicing Service (Peppol BIS 3.0 / UBL 2.1 standards); statutory tax invoices must be issued within 28 days of the supply, contain the compulsory particulars listed in section 24 of the GST Act 1985 (supplier name, IRD number, GST-exclusive amount, GST amount, date, nature of supply, and a statement that GST is included where the total exceeds NZD 1,000), and must be retained electronically for 7 years; GST returns are filed electronically through myIR or EDI channels; the IRD does not operate a stamping or clearance node on the PEPPOL network.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% GST is available under section 11 of the GST Act 1985 for: (a) goods physically exported from New Zealand by the supplier where title passes outside NZ; (b) services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of performance, subject to exclusions for services connected with NZ land, services physically performed on NZ goods, and services supplied to a non-resident physically present in NZ for enjoyment in NZ; and (c) services supplied in a taxable activity that form part of a through-out chain to an offshore principal; for the ISIC 5610 ghost-kitchen/virtual-brand scope: local meal sales fulfilled by a NZ kitchen and paid via UberEats or DoorDash for NZ consumers are standard-rated at 15% GST; international shared-service fees, brand-licence fees, virtual-brand platform commissions, and management or IT back-office fees recharged to an offshore brand owner are zero-rated where the recipient is non-resident and outside NZ at the time of supply; cross-border dispatched meal kits sold to foreign buyers qualify for zero-rating only where contemporaneous export documentation substantiates physical delivery outside New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CUS-EX) filed via the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window
Original Bill of Lading (ocean) or Master and House Airwaybills (air) evidencing physical departure from New Zealand
Commercial Invoice and Packing List identifying the non-resident buyer, Incoterms, HS classification and quantity
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank Foreign Exchange Credit Advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in the IC's bank account
Certificate of Origin (NZ-China FTA, RCEP, CPTPP or NZ-EU FTA) where preferential tariff origin is claimed
Proof of arrival or delivery at the foreign destination (port discharge report, foreign customs entry, or third-party delivery confirmation) supporting the export GST claim
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: IRD audit scrutiny of zero-rating claims is document-intensive and substance-based; failure to substantiate the export chain results in reassessment of output GST at 15% for every affected taxable period, with shortfall penalties under section 141 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 of 20% (failure to take reasonable care), 40% (unacceptable tax position), or 150% (abusive tax position or evasion), plus use-of-money interest accruing daily on unpaid tax; fraudulent zero-rating by a ghost-kitchen/virtual-brand entity is a criminal offence risking fines up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years, in addition to retrospective clawback of all GST refunds and input credits from the date of the original assessment; the 180-day figure in this dossier is the prudential documentary benchmark for inward remittance — New Zealand's GST Act imposes no statutory FX-repatriation term, and a genuine unpaid export debt beyond 180 days will not by itself void zero-rating if the debt remains commercially real, arms-length and fully substantiated.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) / Te Pūtea Matua, with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) sharing AML/CFT supervision; no administered foreign-exchange control authority exists in New Zealand
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full current- and capital-account convertibility for NZD under a free-floating exchange-rate regime (no IMF Article XIV restrictions). No prior central-bank approval is required for inbound capital subscription, trade financing, profit repatriation, dividends, or foreign-currency advances to related parties. The practical friction points are exclusively prudential and AML/CFT-based: bank counterparty due diligence, source-of-funds substantiation, SWIFT payment references, and the tax withholding regime (non-resident withholding tax on interest/dividends). Profit remittance is unfettered once the New Zealand branch/company satisfies IRD return and RWT/NRWT obligations; a New Zealand Inland Revenue (IRD) registration and an NZBN are essential for account opening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Nil statutory surrender or mandatory conversion obligation in New Zealand. Exporters (including delivery-platform settlement receipts from UberEats and DoorDash) may hold USD/AUD/EUR receivables indefinitely in foreign-currency accounts without any prescribed conversion ratio or repatriation timeline. No RBNZ approval threshold has been set for retention of export proceeds; the only reporting requirement is statistical data reported to Statistics NZ on a voluntary/aggregate basis for balance-of-payments compilation, and the automatic exchange of information for CRS/FATCA tax purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: ASB Bank Limited (ASB - Commonwealth Bank of Australia group)
Bank of New Zealand (BNZ - NAB group)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH as a supplementary FX/collection corridor, but LOW as a primary treasury bank. Under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989, only RBNZ-registered banks may conduct the business of banking (including accepting on-demand deposits) in New Zealand; a non-bank fintech/EMI must either partner with a registered bank (pass-through segregated accounts) or restrict itself to licensed money-changer/MSB activities regulated under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act). Cross-border EMIs with an NZ money-service-business license and a licensed trustee arrangement, e.g., Airwallex NZ or Wise Payments NZ, may accept platform settlement from UberEats/DoorDash subject to the platform's own payout-plus/USD rails, but treasury policy should treat the EMI as a transitory clearing node only, with end-of-day sweeps to the Tier-1 NZ bank account. Critical legal constraints: (i) EMI client funds must be held in a designated trust account and are not covered by the RBNZ depositor compensation scheme; (ii) EMI account applications by Cook Islands International Companies are typically declined because the EMT is unable to verify the ultimate beneficial owner at the required AML/CFT standard; (iii) any accumulated settlement must be swept before the EMI's daily balance cap to avoid an unintended 'non-bank borrowing' characterization.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory mandate: New Zealand AML/CFT law does not require a mandatory in-person interview as a rule of law, but every reporting entity must perform satisfactory customer identity verification using reliable, independent source documentation. For the Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) structure, all four major NZ banks (ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac) have a risk-based policy that effectively requires at least one of the following to be completed before account activation: (i) an in-person interview by the Bank's relationship manager with at least one director or the designated agent operating in Auckland; or (ii) a notarized/legal-certified identity pack plus a live video-identification (VTC) interview with a bank-approved certifier; or (iii) a letter of introduction from a NZ-registered law firm or a recognized Cook Islands licensed trustee/registered agent. Registration as an overseas company under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993 and acquisition of an NZBN (provided by the NZ Companies Office) is a de facto precondition before any Tier-1 bank will open the account. Remote-only opening, with zero local contact, is not practicable for a CK_IC that has no NZ resident director; accordingly, the treasury plan must engage an Auckland-based corporate services/guest counsel before banking due diligence. For branch licensing and local director requirements, Foreign LLPs/Foreign companies can avoid a local director only if they appoint a New Zealand-based agent for service of process; however, banks still require a named individual NZ-resident contact with signing authority, which means a non-resident CK_IC must appoint an NZ resident manager under a power of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company (Cook Islands IC) presumption of higher-risk, especially when combined with a delivery business that has digital-only brands and no physical premises visible on corporate records; the bank flags the entity for enhanced due diligence at the initial 'beneficial ownership and control structure' step.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defense package: (i) Cook Islands registered agent certificate plus certificate of good standing issued by the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission within the last 30 days; (ii) a notarized register of members and ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) declaration form naming all natural-person shareholders and their nationality/residence tax IDs; (iii) a solicitor's certification connecting every UBO to the deployment of the inbound capital, including a funds-flow chart from the personal bank account to the CK_IC's Cook Islands bank account (if any) and onward to the NZ treasury account; (iv) a fully executed trust deed (if the CK_IC is held by trust) with the licensed trustee's AML/CFT file references; (v) extract from the NZ Companies Office (NZBN record) evidencing foreign-company registration; and (vi) the ghost kitchen's supply agreements and platform merchant agreements with UberEats and DoorDash to substantiate a low-risk, cashless, delivery-only operational profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP/sanctions screening false positive caused by a UBO sharing a name with a politically exposed person, or the Cook Islands trust being flagged on sanctions/third-party risk lists due to incomplete name matching.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defense package: (i) authoritative identification documents (passport bio page, proof-of-address from a Big-4 utility, notarized copies) for each UBO; (ii) official FBI/Interpol/national-police certificate or expression-of-no-matches output from a recognized sanctions-screening provider; (iii) a short PEP conflit resolution letter from the bank's compliance team, supported by a sworn statutory declaration from the UBO stating non-affiliation with any sanctioned persons; (iv) if the triggering hit is a commercial counterparty (e.g., a supplier or delivery aggregator) rather than a UBO, include the supply-chain contract with the counterparty's own KYB file and end-beneficiary attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth insufficiency: the Cook Islands IC is tax-exempt and the ghost kitchen's projected revenue relies on recurrent capital injections and third-party merchant-advance funding; the bank refuses to accept a 'tax-exempt zone' company at face value.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defense package: (i) audited financial statements of the CK_IC (or parent) for the last two years, prepared under IFRS; (ii) business plan, cash-flow forecast, and a board resolution authorizing the capital contribution to the New Zealand treasury; (iii) source-of-wealth evidence for all initial Pedal/seed capital, including bank statements or securities brokerage statements from the funders, with a formal declaration that no funds are sourced from illicit proceeds; (iv) flight plan of merchant-advance receivables and the settlement flow from UberEats/DoorDash into the NZ bank account (or a licensed EMI); (v) IRD confirmation letter that the CK_IC has no unpaid New Zealand tax obligations or that any liability is under RWT/NRWT, together with a tax clearance certificate where the bank requests it; (vi) placement of ongoing monitoring consent (a standing instruction that the bank may conduct periodic enhanced reviews at the bank's sole discretion).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cook Islands jurisdiction risk on the FATF/GAFI or national watchlist; some NZ banks automatically classify any entity incorporated in the Cook Islands as a higher-risk jurisdiction for money laundering even in the absence of an actual grey-listing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defense package: (i) reliance on the FATF mutual-evaluation report for the Cook Islands (status: improvements made; any residual deficiencies) plus a cover memo from NZ counsel explaining the risk-based mitigation; (ii) demonstrating that the CK_IC's business and intended banking are geographically confined to New Zealand and its trading partners (Australia, US, China) and that the Cook Islands element is purely a holding/tax-exempt structure; (iii) evidence of a genuine tax-and-regulatory nexus in New Zealand: an NZBN, an IRD number, an Auckland registered office for service, and a physical kitchen address; (iv) confirmation that the CK_IC has no bank account in the Cook Islands and that all funds move directly from the UBO's personal account in their country of residence to the NZ account; (v) a consent to the bank's submission of an AML/CFT audit report by a New Zealand licensed auditor, and agreement to disclose any subsequent change in control to the bank within 14 days.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol: (1) originator sends USD/NZD via SWIFT MT103 from the UBO's home-currency or US-domiciled account to the CK_IC's Tier-1 NZ bank account; (2) the payment detail must include the payment reference 'CK_IC SHARE SUBSCRIPTION [date]' or 'CK_IC SUBORDINATED LOAN [date]' and the entity NZBN; (3) the bank will require the UBO to provide a signed board resolution of the CK_IC authorizing the account opening and inward remittance, along with the subordinated loan agreement or the share subscription/allotment resolution; (4) for wires over NZD 100,000, the bank may require the originator's bank to provide a certificate of existence and the UBO's proof of funds (account statement) before credit is applied; (5) if the capital injection is routed via an EMI, the EMI must be an NZ-registered MSB or an RBNZ-licensed bank's partner and must not be the terminal beneficiary; the treasury must control the EMI with a segregated client-fund balance and sweep to the Tier-1 account within 24 hours of settlement. There is no RBNZ exchange-control approval for the capital subscription, but if the overseas transfer acquires 'significant business assets' under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 (asset value > NZD 100 million or sensitive land), Overseas Investment Office (OIO) consent must be obtained before the wiring to avoid downstream clawback of the corporate registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) domestic NZD payments: Bulk Electronic Clearing System (BECS) via the bank's direct-debit/auto-credit service for ingredients, cloud-kitchen rent, and staff payroll; (2) high-value domestic transfers (>NZD 1 million) and interbank treasury sweeps: Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS), the RBNZ real-time gross settlement system, via the bank's commercial-credit grade; (3) cross-border supplier payments (e.g., food-plastic packaging purchased from China/SE Asia): SWIFT MT103 for T/T settlements, with SWIFT MT202/202COV for correspondent-cover only when the beneficiary bank requires a separate cover transfer; (4) equipment/turnkey kitchen-line import: irrevocable documentary letter of credit (L/C) subject to UCP600, issued by the Tier-1 NZ bank, with draft at sight, shipment of CFR/Auckland, and a beneficiary presentation pack including voluminous packing lists, invoices, health certificates, and delivery platform compliance certificates (meeting the Export Control Regulations 2022 for NZ food-safety import; note that the ghost kitchen's imports of food contact packaging require compliance with the Food Act 2014 and the Food (Importer of Food for Human Consumption) Regulations 2021); (5) for recurring payouts owed by the delivery platforms (UberEats, DoorDash), the treasury should establish a dedicated merchant settlement account to receive settlement proceeds, with API links or a daily statement feed to the CK_IC ERP, then programmatically sweep USD to the FX hedge facility forward cover; no NZ statutory restriction exists on the payout rail, but the bank must be notified if settlements are sourced from platform-controlled US-based payment processors (e.g., Stripe/Adyen), because the account title 'CK_IC d/b/a Ghost Kitchen Virtual Brands' must be displayed to the platform and match the bank's KYB record.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (Outright) — NZD/USD and NZD/AUD, term up to 24 months, with bilateral ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a line-of-credit conditional forward facility; no ISDA introduction required by law (a futures broker/client agreement may substitute)
FX Swaps (Swap-out/swap-in, with the bank acting as principal) — for managing the settlement-date mismatch between the UberEats/DoorDash USD payout cycle and the monthly supplier/TTS payment cycle
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) — for matched funding of the CK_IC's subordinated loan in USD swapped into NZD at the company treasury level, and conversely if the op-co uses NZD funding

NDF (Non-Deliverable Forwards) — permissible but discouraged for NZD because NZD is fully deliverable, and discouraged for settlement currencies of the delivery platforms; can only be used for high-inflation target-market currencies where the CK_IC has supplier cost exposure (e.g., SEK/GBP via a clean-secured NDF) and always subject to internal treasury policy

FX Options (call/put European-style) — permitted under the bank's derivatives authorization, used for contingent bid/procurement exposure on kitchen-equipment imports; must be covered by the bank's credit risk documentation and may be booked as a zero-premium collar structure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment - MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 28 working days after the company's annual return date, normally the anniversary of incorporation unless the Registrar sets a different return date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts an automatic NZD 200 penalty; continued non-filing may lead to a notice of intention to remove the company from the New Zealand Companies Register and administrative strike-off, resulting in loss of corporate existence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of directors, shareholders, registered office and beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Furnished with the annual return; any change during the year to directors, shareholders, registered office or beneficial owners must be processed in the statutory registers and reported through the next annual confirmation cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the confirmation obligations is a breach of the Companies Act 1993 and the beneficial ownership regime; directors may be prosecuted and fined up to NZD 10,000, and the company remains exposed to strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a company not exempt under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, financial statements must be filed within the period prescribed for the entity's balance date, commonly within 6 months after balance date; FMC reporting entities must follow the earlier deadlines imposed by the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013. Audit-exempt small and medium private companies that have adopted the available exemption have no annual filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file when required is a continuing offence under the Companies Act 1993; directors may be liable to prosecution and fines, and the Registrar may take corrective action including removal of the company from the register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit is compulsory if the entity is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, or if the company satisfies at least two of the three 'large company' criteria in each of the two preceding accounting periods: consolidated total assets exceeding NZD 60 million, consolidated total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million, and having at least 100 full-time-equivalent employees. A smaller private company may nevertheless need an audit if the shareholders have not unanimously adopted the annual audit exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ GAAP, comprising New Zealand equivalents of International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS) and the External Reporting Board's Accounting Standards Framework, including the Tier 2 Reduced Disclosure Regime and the Tier 3/Tier 4 simplified frameworks for eligible smaller for-profit entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies Act 1993 and the Companies (Register of Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2017, the company must maintain a register of beneficial owners and file current particulars in the annual return. Any share transfer that changes beneficial ownership must be recorded in the register of members and in the beneficial ownership register promptly, and updated in the subsequent annual confirmation to the Companies Office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (shareholders', directors' and committee meetings)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (resident company headline rate under Income Tax Act 2007, Part A; non-resident IC deriving only foreign-source income may be outside the NZ tax net)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No NZ territorial tax holidays or free-zone exemptions are available to an IC; the 28% headline rate is effectively neutral for offshore activities. Statutory preferences include the 15% R&D tax credit (s LZ 8 and subpart DP), immediate deduction for certain commercial fit-out under the depreciation rules, and full deductibility for arm's-length royalties/fees paid to counterparties. A 'Tax-Exempt Zone' designation does not exempt or reduce NZ corporate income tax unless the IC is treated as non-resident and earns no NZ-source income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: unlimited (Indefinite carryforward subject to shareholder continuity of at least 49%; for a foreign-owned IC, losses may be non-deductible if the IC is treated as non-resident and has no NZ-source gross income)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed through the Inland Revenue 'myIR' secure portal or a commercial provider using IRD e-file / Business Gateway
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 must be filed by the 7th day of the 7th month after the balance date (e.g. 7 October for a 31 March balance date). Terminal tax is payable on 7 February (or 7 April for provisional taxpayers).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income from business operations, including UberEats and DoorDash settlement payouts, delivery partner charges, and virtual brand royalty/franchise revenue attributable to New Zealand.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC must include only New Zealand-source income. Foreign-source trading income and offshore virtual brand royalties are excluded unless the company is resident or has a fixed base in NZ.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary and necessary business expenses directly incurred in deriving taxable income, including food and packaging costs, rent, utilities, equipment leases, salaries, technology platform fees, and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses incurred in producing the New Zealand taxable income. Apportion shared overhead on a reasonable 40/60 or turnover-based formula and maintain a contemporaneous apportionment certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from previous years that are offset against current-year assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC may utilise NZ losses only if the loss arose from NZ-source activities and continuity was maintained; if the IC is wholly foreign-owned and not tax-resident, the loss pool is generally unavailable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable income after deducting total expenses and applying available loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net taxable income for a non-resident consists of the gross NZ-source income less directly attributable deductible expenses; do not net foreign-source losses against NZ-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate tax liability computed at 28% of net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident IC, this box must reflect only treaty-compliant NZ business profits, and any withholding tax credits (RWT, AIL) should be claimed in the credits section.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resident withholding tax (RWT), provisional tax paid, valued-added tax adjustments, and any foreign tax credits attachable to NZ tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach only arm's-length tax credit vouchers. A non-resident cannot claim imputation credits unless the shares are held in a New Zealand resident portfolio; instead, the appropriate treaty relief is applied via NRWT protocol.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Director or authorised agent confirms the return is true and complete, and records the date and signature.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The principal director must personally sign even if outside New Zealand; a New Zealand agent may co-sign, but the director retains criminal liability for false declarations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty NZ$250 for the first day and NZ$50 for each 28-day period, capped at NZ$1,000. Late payment penalties accrue at 1% of the unpaid tax immediately, followed by further incremental penalties and interest (use of money rates). Deliberate false returns trigger shortfall penalties up to 150% of the tax shortfall and potential criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends paid by a New Zealand company to a non-resident shareholder; may be reduced to 15%, 10%, or 5% under an applicable double taxation agreement (e.g. US/Canada/Australia treaty rates).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced NRWT, the non-resident shareholder must (i) complete the Inland Revenue 'NRWT rate certificate' application (IR67E/IR67F equivalent), (ii) attach a current Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home-country tax authorities, and (iii) provide the beneficial ownership declaration to the New Zealand paying company and the IRD before the dividend declaration date. The paying company must retain the certificate file, and the annual IR67 reconciliation must identify the reduced-rate class. The IRD may ask for a certificate of residence within the specific DTA, an explanation of the 10% ownership threshold, and a statement that the shareholder is entitled to benefits under the LOB/PPT article.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT rates are 15% for interest and 15% for royalties. Treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 10% or 0% and royalties to 5% or 10% depending on the residence state and beneficial ownership. For interest paid to unrelated lenders, an Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may be substituted for NRWT where the debenture is issued to a non-resident and the conditions of the Income Tax Act 2007, Part T are met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10 million aggregate cross-border related-party controlled transactions in an income year trigger the mandatory contemporaneous New Zealand transfer pricing documentation (Local File/Master File). OECD Country-by-Country Reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue over NZD 1.14 billion (EUR 750 million).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not execute Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the IRD applies BEPS-consistent substance requirements through controlled foreign company (CFC) rules, the general anti-avoidance rule (Income Tax Act 2007, s BG 1 and Part FE), and the Limitation of Benefits/Principal Purpose Test under NZ DTAs. An IC labelled 'Tax-Exempt Zone' will be disregarded for treaty/tax purposes if it lacks physical presence, payroll, local board meetings, and real business decision-making. The ghost-kitchen operator must maintain board minutes evidencing operational control over franchise food-preparation contracts, delivery-platform agreements, and profit repatriation; office or kitchen premises; a local New Zealand bank account; and functional employees who manage order flow, supplier contracts, and compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Deliberate Concealment of Turnover
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating or omitting UberEats and DoorDash settlement amounts received by the ghost-kitchen virtual brand, destroying point-of-sale/transaction records, or invoicing franchise royalties through a shell bank account to avoid taxable profit recognition in New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil shortfall penalty up to 150% of the tax shortfall plus late payment penalties and use-of-money interest. Criminal prosecution under Tax Administration Act 1994, s 143A may result in judgment fines up to NZ$50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years, plus forfeiture of profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false IR4 returns or participate in concealment may be personally prosecuted, have the corporate veil pierced under Companies Act 1993 ss 382-385, be disqualified from managing companies for up to 5 years, be subject to travel restrictions in IRD asset-preservation cases, and be jointly and severally liable for unpaid PAYE/GST and shortfall penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering the IC solely as a 'tax-exempt zone' vehicle with no New Zealand employees, no kitchen/premises, and no real management control, while the entire ghost-kitchen revenue stream is booked offshore and franchise/royalty payments are stripped out to a related non-resident entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterisation of the entire arrangement under s BG 1 and s GA 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007; denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test; re-allocation of profits to New Zealand; TP adjustment plus a shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the resulting additional tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause the company to operate without economic substance may be jointly liable for the adjusted corporate tax debt where the company is unable to pay. The Court may order restitution, impose a civil penalty, and disqualify the director from managing any company in New Zealand.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to enrol and discharge obligations under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 where the ghost-kitchen IC provides financial services, conducts non-face-to-face transactions with high-volume delivery-platform payouts, or ignores source-of-funds documentation for franchise or investor cash inflows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML/CFT civil penalties of up to NZ$4 million for a body corporate and NZ$1 million for individual directors, plus criminal liability for knowingly laundering proceeds, imprisonment up to 7 years, confiscation of assets, and public enforcement publication.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers are personally liable for a failure to implement and maintain AML/CFT programmes; culpable conduct may lead to imprisonment up to 7 years, disqualification, and civil costs, and the Court may order disclosure of personal assets for confiscation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Imputation Credit Mismatch
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to non-resident shareholders without deducting NRWT, incorrectly claiming imputation credits on a non-resident-held dividend, or failing to file the IR67 annual non-resident withholding tax reconciliation for royalty and interest payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer company is assessed for the entire unwithheld NRWT, plus a non-declaration penalty of up to NZ$1,000, a 150% shortfall penalty where the failure is intentional, and late payment penalties over the full unpaid amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director is jointly and severally liable for unpaid NRWT and penalties to the extent they knowingly directed or participated in the dividend/royalty distribution, and may be barred from leaving New Zealand pending payment, with seizure of personal assets under tax recovery provisions.
